info.title: Releem API
info.description:
Manage servers and customers, inspect database diagnostics and retrieve performance metrics.

All example identifiers, addresses, names, query fingerprints and values are fictional. Replace them with values from your account.

Authenticate with an API token in the Releem-Secret-Key header. Internal Bubble integrations can instead supply an admin bearer token together with Releem-Bubble-Auth: true and the target user's Releem-Api-Key. Invalid, expired or revoked credentials return 401.

Errors use a JSON error object containing code, message and optional details.

get.description:
List event summaries for a server accessible to the authenticated user. Both time bounds are required and inclusive. Timezone offsets are converted to UTC; timestamps without a timezone are interpreted as UTC. Time bounds have one-second precision.

Results are ordered by event time descending, then event ID descending. Pagination is applied after server and time filters. The response contains `items`, without a total count; advance `offset` until a page contains fewer than `limit` items. Offset pagination does not freeze a snapshot: new events can shift subsequent pages. The response includes personal is_viewed state. GET never changes it; acknowledge only successfully displayed events with POST /v1/servers/{id}/events/viewed.

get.description: Server metadata with every health and security check of the latest report, passing or failing, in display order. Each check carries its result and catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link, severity and group. An absent security report produces an empty security_checks object. Malformed or ambiguous security reports and unmapped failure codes return 422 invalid_source_data. Includes the current unapplied configuration-change count and the preparation status, update time and estimated availability of the next configuration. These fields do not describe progress of an agent task.

Every health check of the server's latest report, in display order, with its result, value and catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link and group. MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL servers have different checks. A check the catalog has no entry for is listed last with null texts.

Every security check of the server's latest security snapshot, in display order, with its result, value and catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link, severity and group. MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL have separate check names. Account findings can have a null value when account details are unavailable. Unknown future named checks retain their reported values and have null catalog texts. Malformed or ambiguous security reports and unmapped failure codes return 422 invalid_source_data.

Every configuration state of one server, applied or not, newest first — the list Releem Platform shows. Each row is one state of a configuration, so a configuration that was applied or rolled back appears once per state; `configuration_id` groups them. All states are returned unless `limit` is given. With `latest=true` only the server's current state is returned — its newest state, the first row of the full list — or an empty list when the server has none.

schema.title: Limit

schema.title: Latest

get.description: Return full details for the latest fully or partially applied configuration and the second state of application history. Latest is ordered by applied_timestamp then configuration_status_id, descending, and includes application statuses 1 and 2. Previous is the second row ordered by max(timestamp, applied_timestamp) then configuration_status_id, descending; history includes every nonzero application status and the initial state of the first configuration. These are different selectors, so latest and previous can identify the same state. A missing selection is null. Read access to the server is required. This operation does not generate summaries or modify stored state.

get.description: Retrieve query execution statistics for a time window. The window is `[start_date, start_date + period)`, `[start_date, end_date)`, or the last `period` up to now without `start_date`. The start is included and the end is excluded in every mode. An explicit `end_date` requires `start_date` and overrides `period`; it must be later than the start. Bounds use second precision. Percentages are relative to every query that passes the filters, so with `schema_name` they are shares of that schema. The period is a positive integer optionally followed by `m` (minutes), `h` (hours), or `d` (days); a bare integer means days. Other suffixes are rejected.

parameters.name: period

schema.description: Positive integer with optional m (minutes), h (hours), d (days); bare numbers mean days
schema.title: Period

parameters.description: Positive integer with optional m (minutes), h (hours) or d (days). A bare integer means days. Default: 1 day. An explicit end_date overrides this duration; the period must still be valid.

parameters.name: end_date

schema.description: Exclusive window end, ISO date or datetime; requires start_date and overrides period
schema.title: End Date

parameters.description: Exclusive end, ISO date or datetime. Requires start_date, must be later, and overrides period.

schema.description: IANA time zone for start_date and end_date without an offset
schema.title: Timezone

get.description: List available metrics for one server, including the server-scoped item ID needed for `GET /v1/servers/{id}/metrics/byId/{itemid}`.

Average, minimum and maximum of every metric of one server over a window, computed from hourly trends in one read. A metric without trend data in the window is listed with null values. `start_time` and `end_time` are required; a reversed range is rejected with 400 `invalid_time_range` and a window longer than 366 days with 400 `time_range_too_wide`. The window includes `start_time` and excludes `end_time`, so adjacent windows do not overlap; request two windows to compare a period with the previous one. Values that are not finite numbers are returned as null.

parameters.name: metric_name
parameters.description: The name of the metric to retrieve

schema.description: Aggregation function: avg, sum, min, max
schema.title: Aggregation

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Grouping interval: a positive number followed by m, h or d (e.g. 5m, 1h, 1d)

parameters.name: use_trends

schema.description: Use hourly trend summaries instead of raw samples
schema.title: Use Trends

parameters.description: Use hourly aggregated metric data instead of raw samples

get.description: Retrieve metric data for one server's metric, looked up by metric name. Unlike the deprecated `GET /v1/metrics/{metric_name}`, `start_time` and `end_time` are required and a reversed range is rejected with 400 `invalid_time_range`. Request parameters are validated before any data is read: `aggregation` must be one of the members below and applies only together with `interval` or `use_trends` (otherwise 400 `aggregation_requires_interval`); `interval` must look like `5m`, `1h` or `1d` (otherwise 400 `invalid_interval`). A window may span at most 31 days of raw samples, or 366 days with `use_trends=true` (otherwise 400 `time_range_too_wide`). Not every metric is aggregated into hourly trends; `use_trends=true` for an item that has no trend rows returns 400 `trends_not_available` rather than an empty series.

An `itemid` that belongs to a different server returns 404. Request parameters are validated before any data is read: `aggregation` must be one of the members below and applies only together with `interval` or `use_trends` (otherwise 400 `aggregation_requires_interval`); `interval` must look like `5m`, `1h` or `1d` (otherwise 400 `invalid_interval`). A window may span at most 31 days of raw samples, or 366 days with `use_trends=true` (otherwise 400 `time_range_too_wide`). Not every metric is aggregated into hourly trends; `use_trends=true` for an item that has no trend rows returns 400 `trends_not_available` rather than an empty series.

Schema checks from the most recent completed run for one server. A null `timestamp` means no run has completed schema checks yet. A non-null `timestamp` with an empty `items` list means the filters matched nothing in that run — which equals "the run found nothing" only when no filters were applied. Each result includes its type code object, title, description and documentation link when the catalog has a definition for this server DBMS. Unknown types keep their original id and raw data, with null display texts.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by schema check type. Matched on the canonical form, so `unused_index` and the stored `UNUSED_INDEX_NEW` select the same checks. The endpoint returns these check types only: `missing_primary_key`, `unused_index`, `duplicate_index`, `auto_increment`, `collation`, `character_set`, `table_engine` and `table_fragmentation`; any other value matches nothing

MySQL/MariaDB: `1` On-premise, `2` AWS RDS, `3` Docker, `4` GCP Cloud SQL, `5` Azure. PostgreSQL: `101` On-premise, `102` AWS RDS, `103` Docker, `104` GCP Cloud SQL, `105` Azure. Null when unavailable; clients must tolerate additional codes.

memory_limit.title: Memory Limit
memory_limit.description: Effective memory limit in bytes. Returns the explicit server override when present (including 0); when the override is NULL, falls back to the agent-reported mysql_memory_limit, already in bytes. Null when neither value is available. No conversion or rounding is applied to the fallback.

users.title: Users
users.description: Users with access to the server.

releem_score.title: Releem Score
releem_score.description: Server health score from 0 to 100; higher values indicate better health.

status.title: Status
status.description: Server monitoring status: `active` or `inactive`; null when unavailable.

instance_type.title: Instance Type
instance_type.description: Code object with the original id and its display name. Database deployment code, returned as a string. MySQL/MariaDB: `1` On-premise, `2` AWS RDS, `3` Docker, `4` GCP Cloud SQL, `5` Azure. PostgreSQL: `101` On-premise, `102` AWS RDS, `103` Docker, `104` GCP Cloud SQL, `105` Azure. Null when unavailable; clients must tolerate additional codes.

memory_limit.title: Memory Limit
memory_limit.description: Effective memory limit in bytes. Returns the explicit server override when present (including 0); when the override is NULL, falls back to the agent-reported mysql_memory_limit, already in bytes. Null when neither value is available. No conversion or rounding is applied to the fallback.

agent_up_to_date.title: Agent Up To Date
agent_up_to_date.description: Whether the installed Releem Agent is the current version: `false` when an update is available, null when not yet evaluated.

unapplied_recommendations_count.title: Unapplied Recommendations Count
unapplied_recommendations_count.description: Number of configuration changes still unapplied in the latest server report. Zero means no unapplied changes; null means the count is unavailable. This is not the number of recommendation cards.

configuration_preparation_status.title: Configuration Preparation Status
configuration_preparation_status.description: Code object describing preparation of a future configuration, independently of the application status of an existing configuration. Known IDs: 1 analyzing metrics, 2 preparing configuration. Unknown IDs retain their value with name=null; null when unavailable.

configuration_preparation_updated_at.title: Configuration Preparation Updated At
configuration_preparation_updated_at.description: Time the configuration preparation status was updated, as an ISO 8601 datetime in UTC with an explicit offset. Null when unavailable.

next_configuration_at.title: Next Configuration At
next_configuration_at.description: Estimated time the next configuration will be available, as an ISO 8601 datetime in UTC with an explicit offset. Present only while preparation status is 2 and the schedule is available. A past value means the estimate has elapsed; it is not a guarantee that generation has finished. Null for other stages or an unavailable schedule.

health_checks.title: Health Checks
health_checks.description: Health check results. Numeric value fields include their display units (%, min, s, count); no separate result unit field. Fractional values are rounded to one decimal (decimal half-up); integers keep their integer form. No scaling. Null, boolean and structured values retain their existing forms. Values without a suffix retain their type with the same fractional rounding. Internal scoring is unchanged. Public health results omit open_files_limit, mysql_restart_service, mysql_conf_dir_or_rds_parameter_group, releem_conf_dir, latency_collection, table_cache_pressure and table_definition_cache_pressure. Internal results and failure flags remain unchanged; other unknown checks are retained.

security_checks_score.title: Security Checks Score
security_checks_score.description: Security score from the latest report; null when unavailable.

security_checks.title: Security Checks
security_checks.description: All recognized security checks keyed by check name, in display order. Values follow ServerHealthCheckResult.

current_task.description: Current agent task; null when no current task is available.

users.title: Users
users.description: Users with access to the server. Empty when access information is unavailable.

configuration_status_id.title: Configuration Status Id
configuration_status_id.description: Configuration state identifier; use it in the configuration detail endpoint.

configuration_id.title: Configuration Id
configuration_id.description: Configuration identifier. Multiple application states can refer to the same configuration.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Configuration state time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

configuration_timestamp.title: Configuration Timestamp
configuration_timestamp.description: Configuration creation time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

applied_status.title: Applied Status
applied_status.description: Code object with the original id and its display name. Application status: `0` not applied (history display: Skipped), `1` applied, `2` partially applied, `3` rolled back.

applied_timestamp.title: Applied Timestamp
applied_timestamp.description: Application time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds; `0` when never applied.

recommendations_changes.title: Recommendations Changes
recommendations_changes.description: Number of configuration changes recommended by the analysis; null when unavailable.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Configuration variable values; null when unavailable.

configuration_metrics.title: Configuration Metrics
configuration_metrics.description: Configuration evaluation metrics; null when unavailable.

is_first.title: Is First
is_first.description: Whether this is the initial configuration.

required_restart.title: Required Restart
required_restart.description: Restart requirement: `0` no restart required, `1` restart required; null when unknown.

items.title: Items
items.description: One entry per server that has a configuration.

avg.title: Avg
avg.description: Mean of the hourly averages in the window; null without data.

min.title: Min
min.description: Lowest hourly minimum in the window; null without data.

max.title: Max
max.description: Highest hourly maximum in the window; null without data.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: One entry per metric of the server.

itemid.title: Itemid
itemid.description: Server-scoped metric identifier; use it in the metric-by-ID endpoint.

description.title: Description
examples: The number of statements executed by the server

value_type.title: Value Type
value_type.description: Metric value type: `0` floating-point number, `3` unsigned integer.

role.description: Server access role: `viewer` for read-only access or `editor` for write access.
Server access role: `viewer` for read-only access or `editor` for write access.

users.title: Users
users.description: Users to grant access to the server. Required; may be an empty array.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: Subscription start time in ISO 8601 format.

valid_to.title: Valid To
valid_to.description: Subscription expiration time in ISO 8601 format.

number_servers.title: Number Servers
number_servers.description: Number of servers included in the subscription.

memory_limit.title: Memory Limit
memory_limit.description: Memory limit in bytes, as a nonnegative multiple of 1048576 (1 MiB). Maximum 2251799812636672 bytes, corresponding to signed INT maximum 2147483647 MiB. Zero is stored and returned as zero.

mysql_config.title: Mysql Config
mysql_config.description: MySQL configuration variables as a JSON object. Replaces the previous configuration override.

status.title: Status
status.description: Query optimization status code. Known codes: `0` queued, `1` collecting query plan, `2` analyzing, `3` analysis failed, `4` generated, `5` Discovered (ready for optimization), `6` Discovered, `7` Evaluating (application detected and awaiting evaluation), `8` Evaluating (evaluation measured improvement), `9` Evaluating (evaluation measured no improvement), `10` completed, `11` preserved, `100` dismissed. Clients must tolerate additional numeric codes. Updating this field does not change the status timestamp.

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: Agent task identifier belonging to this server. At least one of status or task_id is required.

deadlock_type.title: Deadlock Type
deadlock_type.description: Code object with the original id and its display name. Deadlock type: `0` other, `1` concurrent UPDATE, `2` SELECT FOR UPDATE, `3` auto-increment lock, `4` gap lock, `5` insert-intention lock, `6` competing INSERT on a primary key, `7` primary/secondary index lock-order conflict. Null when unavailable.

txn1.title: Txn1
txn1.description: First transaction details, encoded as text.

txn2.title: Txn2
txn2.description: Second transaction details, encoded as text.

max_active_time.title: Max Active Time
max_active_time.description: Maximum active transaction duration in seconds; `-1` or null when unknown.

is_viewed.title: Is Viewed
is_viewed.description: Whether this authenticated user explicitly acknowledged displaying this deadlock. GET does not change the mark.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: Last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: Subscription start time in ISO 8601 format.

valid_to.title: Valid To
valid_to.description: Subscription expiration time in ISO 8601 format.

plan_id.title: Plan Id
plan_id.description: Subscription plan identifier from the billing catalog.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: Last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

subscription.description: Customer subscription; null when no subscription exists.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Whether the check reports a problem.

value.title: Value
value.description: Public numeric health-check values are display strings with the unit directly attached, without a space (%, min, s, count), for example 95.5%. Public fractional values are rounded to one decimal (decimal half-up); integer values retain their integer form. No scaling is added. Values without a known suffix retain their type and use the same fractional rounding. Nonnumeric strings, booleans and structured values keep their original form; missing values stay null. Internal scoring and security-check values are unchanged. PostgreSQL lock_conflicts uses count, correcting Bubble's percent label.

title.title: Title
title.description: Human-readable name of the check, or null when the catalog has no entry for it.

short_description.title: Short Description
short_description.description: One-line summary of the check for a table row, or null.
examples: How often a cached thread is reused.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the check examines and why it matters, or null when the catalog has no entry. Plain text; it contains no values of a particular server.
examples: Shows how often a new connection reuses a cached thread instead of creating one.

learn_more_url.title: Learn More Url
learn_more_url.description: Documentation link for the check, or null when there is none.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Importance of a security check: `critical`, `high` or `moderate`. Null for health checks and for checks without a catalog entry.

group.title: Group
group.description: Section the check is listed under, or null when it has none.

bearerAuth.description: Admin/Bubble bearer token. Enter the raw token only; Swagger adds 'Bearer ' automatically. Used with Releem-Bubble-Auth + Releem-Api-Key.

apiToken.name: Releem-Secret-Key
apiToken.description: Releem API token. Use this authentication method for API clients.

bubbleAuth.name: Releem-Bubble-Auth
bubbleAuth.description: Internal Bubble authentication flag. Enter true; requires bearerAuth and userApiKey.

userApiKey.name: Releem-Api-Key
userApiKey.description: Target user's API key for internal Bubble authentication; requires bearerAuth and bubbleAuth.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: Time series and averages of a server's system and database metrics.

tags.name: Query Analytics
tags.description: Query statistics of a server, recommendations for one query, and processlist captures.

tags.name: Query Optimizations
tags.description: Queries tracked for optimization on a server and their EXPLAIN-based recommendations. A new record uses the request processing time as its status timestamp; updating a record does not change it.

tags.name: Recommendations
tags.description: Recommendation cards across servers and for one server, and their status.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Events of a server and marking them viewed.

tags.name: Deadlocks
tags.description: Deadlocks captured on a server and marking them viewed.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Agent tasks of a server: history, one task, and queueing a new one. A new task uses the request processing time as its status timestamp.

tags.name: Deprecated
tags.description: Endpoints kept for existing clients. Use the replacement named in each description.
